soundness_flags.label: def:face-complete-prior / thm:complete-saddle-duality
soundness_flags.one_line: The symbol definition lets F* include any face receiving positive mass, whereas def:face-complete-prior requires prior positive mass on that face's relative interior; these are not equivalent and the claimed nonempty Pi^fc needs one definition.

soundness_flags.label: oeq:unbalanced-no-index-witness
soundness_flags.one_line: “Interval-certified prior” is undefined: neither Pi^fc nor the exchange certificate defines a certificate attached to a prior with exact zero primal-dual gap.

soundness_flags.label: prop:centrosymmetric-reduction
soundness_flags.one_line: On O_p^(4), equality of the objectives follows directly from defining O_p^(4) as games with exactly the comparator's domain, covariance, and endpoint maps; this comparison portion is not an independent proposition.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:tie-uniform-lan-transfer
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Uniform two-sided Le Cam convergence and the joint statistic/estimated-game total-variation approximation are assumed, not derived from the original sampling model.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The feasible regret bound is conditional on ass:uniform-lan, ass:joint-risk-transfer, the stated kappa-bounded primitives, and alpha_n, epsilon_n tending to zero.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats fully differentiable non-centrosymmetric and directionally differentiable centrosymmetric cases as non-nested cases; Assumption 5(i) imposes convexity and centrosymmetry, and the conclusion leaves directional differentiability without centrosymmetry for future work.
Theorem 1 assumes a convex centrosymmetric parameter space and gives a minimax-regret rule under normal errors without restricting the class of decision rules.

Definition 2 requires an open set with lower endpoint below zero and upper endpoint above zero; Theorem 3 gives infinitely many MMR rules and qualified one-index threshold failures under additional centered assumptions.
Theorem 1 applies mirror descent/Hedge to a simplex over a finite list of decision rules and outputs an epsilon-minimax mixture.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops asymptotic optimality theory for statistical treatment rules in smooth parametric and semiparametric models.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: With a Gaussian limit, full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for standard bootstrap consistency in the stated directional-differentiability framework.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops an adding-dropping exchange method for convex semi-infinite programming and proves finite approximate-optimality under its stated conditions.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies uniform inference for value functions formed by marginal optimization and emphasizes their directional rather than full Hadamard differentiability.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define F* uniformly using relative-interior support, then state and prove the finite convex-combination argument yielding one face-complete least-favorable prior.
Replace “interval-certified prior” with an explicit finite rational prior, its Bayes rule, the equality R(delta)=b(pi), and a specified interval-arithmetic enclosure proving those equalities.

Move the tautological O_p^(4) objective identity to the sanity discussion and replace the proposition with a non-definitional comparison, such as a proved primitive inclusion or a derived finite-support/face bound on the actual published overlap.
For the transfer theorem, exhibit one concrete original experiment whose sample split verifies gamma_n and alpha_n, so the conditional feasible bound has a directly usable causal application.

recommended_next_step: Revise the three statement-definition defects, retain the conditional transfer scope, then resubmit this field-tier asymmetric nonsmooth saddle kernel for Stage 0.
